finding.claim: Unauthenticated SSRF: the POST 'feed' parameter is passed directly to file_get_contents() with no auth check, scheme or host allowlist, or IP filtering. An attacker can make the server request internal HTTP targets such as cloud metadata at http://169.254.169.254/ or localhost services. file_get_contents also accepts other wrappers such as file:// and ftp://. The response body is not returned, but strlen($xml) is echoed. That gives a size oracle and a way to probe whether internal hosts or ports respond.

trace.note: Entry: any POST request with a 'feed' param; the require_admin() defined at line 4 is not called on this branch
User-controlled URL passed straight to file_get_contents (sink)
strlen of the fetched body is echoed back, giving a response-size oracle

finding.guards_checked: No require_admin() call, no parse_url, scheme or host allowlist, no private-IP or DNS-rebinding check, and no redirect limit. The only auth helper is defined at line 4 and used only on the set_webhook branch. Not reported: set_webhook at import.php:17-24 does curl_init($_POST['set_webhook']) with no URL validation, but it is gated by require_admin() at line 18. It was excluded as an admin-only action under the audit's privilege rule. The $_GET['page'] handling at line 27 uses basename() and is a local file read, not SSRF.

verdict.reason: import.php:11-13 passes $_POST['feed'] straight to file_get_contents() and echoes strlen(), with no require_admin() call (defined at lines 4-9 but only used at line 18) and no URL validation.
